key_insight: Extractive summarization can be formulated as a combinatorial (Ising/QUBO) optimization and efficiently executed on a CMOS Ising machine, enabling low‑power, low‑latency sentence selection without large CPU/GPU costs.
problem_solved: Modern extractive summarization models are accurate but rely on energy‑hungry CPUs/GPUs, making real‑time inference in resource‑constrained environments impractical; this work shows a hardware‑efficient alternative.
method: Map the McDonald-style extractive summarization objective (maximize relevance, minimize redundancy) to a QUBO/Ising formulation where binary spin variables represent sentence selection.
Implement and solve the Ising model on a CMOS Ising machine (specialized hardware for combinatorial optimization) to perform fast, low‑power inference.
Compare solution quality and system metrics (accuracy vs. redundancy tradeoff, energy, latency) against conventional CPU/GPU baselines to validate feasibility.
impact: Provides a practical path to deploy extractive summarization in energy- and latency‑sensitive settings (edge devices, real‑time services) and demonstrates the viability of specialized Ising hardware for combinatorial NLP tasks.
visual_elements: Diagram: mapping from document → sentence nodes → binary spins (Ising variables) showing relevance and redundancy terms
Hardware block: CMOS Ising machine schematic with data flow from sentence embeddings to spin configuration
Chart: tradeoff plot comparing energy and latency (Ising HW vs CPU/GPU) against summarization quality
Example: short document with highlighted sentences selected by the Ising solver vs baseline model
paper_title: Extractive summarization on a CMOS Ising machine
paper_authors: Ziqing Zeng, Abhimanyu Kumar, Chris H. Kim, Ulya R. Karpuzcu, Sachin S. Sapatnekar
